name: TPA6120A2
type: Current-feedback stereo headphone driver, class AB
tagline: TI's 2004 CFA headphone driver: 128 dB dynamic range, 1300 V/µs; inside the Xonar Essence STX and many DAC/amps.

lineage.note: Sole source. SLOS431 first issued March 2004; Rev A July 2014, Rev B February 2015.
DIYers simulate with THS6012 models and treat them as interchangeable; shared die unconfirmed by TI.

part_numbers.note: 20-pin PowerPAD SOIC (HSOIC); tube of 25 / 2000 reel. Mouser 595-TPA6120A2DWPR, LCSC C70439.
14-pin VQFN PowerPAD; 250 / 3000 reel. Mouser 595-TPA6120A2RGYT. −40 °C to 85 °C, NiPdAu.
Legacy 'G4' green variant, not orderable today; probably discontinued. Known from Octopart mirror.
Forum shorthand only; no orderable part without the A2 suffix exists.

key_specs.value: Unconfirmed; 80 mW into 600 Ω at ±12 V (Soomal)

reputation.summary: TI's ready-made current-feedback headphone driver, ubiquitous in the 2009–2016 PC-audio and Chinese DAC/amp boom and still used by SMSL, Sabaj, FiiO, Shanling (M5 Ultra) and Rupert Neve (RNHP). Prized for drive, low noise and low cost. Soomal tested 10–16 products: results depend on implementation. Series output resistors give ~10 Ω output impedance; good composite designs measure very well.
typical_uses: Sound cards: Xonar Essence STX/ST, Sound Blaster ZxR/E5/X7/G5, Musiland
Portables: Sony PHA-1/PHA-2, OPPO HA-2, FiiO E9/X7-AM5, Topping NX3
Desktop: SMSL SAP-9/M20/DO400, Sabaj A20d, Aiyima DAC-A10, WiiM Ultra
Current buffer in VFA–CFA composites (OPA1602/OPA1612, OPA2134, NE5532)
DIY headphone amps (pavouk.org, Cocoacrumbs, Head-Fi, AMB)
caveats: TI's reference circuit uses series output resistors: ~10 Ω output impedance on Sony PHA-1 (ASR) and Roland UA-M10.
Huge drive can damage IEMs or low-impedance headphones if gain is not limited (Soomal, Musiland Monitor 01 PS).
Wide-band CFA: sensitive to layout, feedback resistor and capacitive load; composites need careful compensation (TI E2E).
SMD only (PowerPAD SOIC-20 / VQFN-14); no DIP swap; PowerPAD must be soldered to thermal vias.
Needs ±5 V to ±15 V rails; portables need boost converters. Soomal: sounds better at higher supply.

counterfeit_notes: No counterfeit reports found. Loose chips mostly reach buyers via AliExpress/Taobao modules with unverifiable supply chains. Buy from TI, Mouser (595-TPA6120A2DWPR / 595-TPA6120A2RGYT), DigiKey or LCSC (C70439); check the TI mark, date code and intact PowerPAD.

claims_confirmed: SLOS431B dated 'March 2004 – revised February 2015'; no SLOS431C (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tpa6120a2.pdf).
SLOS431A revised July 2014; original SLOS431 March 2004 (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tpa6120a2.pdf).
Up to 128 dB dynamic range, current-feedback class AB (https://www.ti.com/product/TPA6120A2).
1300 V/µs; ±5 V to ±15 V; 0.9 µVrms output noise at G=1, 16 Ω (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tpa6120a2.pdf, https://www.mouser.com/en/new/texas-instruments/ti-tpa6120a2-amplifiers/).
DWP, DWPR, RGYT, RGYR active; −40 °C to 85 °C; NiPdAu (https://www.ti.com/product/TPA6120A2/part-details/TPA6120A2RGYT).
DigiKey and Octopart DWPG4 mirrors carry the old-template datasheet (https://media.digikey.com/pdf/Data%20Sheets/Texas%20Instruments%20PDFs/TPA6120A2.pdf).
OPA1602 + TPA6120A2 composites discussed on diyAudio (https://www.diyaudio.com/community/threads/high-performance-opa1602-tpa6120a2-composite-headphone-amplifier.347613/page-3).
